title: Dolly Parton’s Catalog Surges by 1,143% in Streams After Her Death
summary: Here's a rundown of her full impact on the Sept. 5-dated Billboard charts.
contentText:
Dolly Parton ’s musical catalog experienced a vault of 1,143% in official on-demand streams in the United States week over week following her Aug. 25 death , according to Luminate.

Related

Dolly Parton Returns to Billboard 200 Top 5, Notching Second-Highest-Charting Album Ever

Dolly Parton’s ‘Jolene’ & ‘I Will Always Love You’ Recordings Become Top 40 Hot 100 Hits for the First Time

How Much Is Dolly Parton’s Catalog Worth?

In the Aug. 21-27 tracking period, Parton’s music was streamed 116.7 million times in the U.S., up from 9.4 million streams the previous week (Aug. 14-20).

Parton’s songs Aug. 21-27 vs. Aug. 14-20 also accumulated 48.9 million radio audience impressions — up 1,632% from 2.8 million; earned 150,000 equivalent album units — a gain of 1,428% from 10,000; and sold 144,000 downloads — an 8,084% boost from 2,000.

Of those 150,000 units earned, 27,000 are in album sales, marking a 2,556% growth from 1,000 the week before.

On Aug. 26, the day after her death, Parton was the most streamed artist in the U.S., with 54.3 million streams occurring that day; the next closest act, Drake, earned 41.9 million.

As a result of those gains, Parton’s music surges on the latest Billboard charts, dated Sept. 5. As previously reported , it’s paced by a No. 16 reentry for “Jolene” on the Billboard Hot 100 , while Ultimate Dolly Parton returns to the Billboard 200 at No. 5.

“Jolene,” which originally reached No. 60 on the Hot 100 in 1974, scores a new high via 10.2 million chart-eligible streams, 5.5 million in airplay audience and nearly 15,000 sold Aug. 21-27. It also returns at No. 7 on Hot Country Songs and debuts at the same position on the all-genre Streaming Songs list and places at No. 2 on the Digital Song Sales chart.

“I Will Always Love You” is the song that beats “Jolene” on Digital Song Sales, bowing at No. 1 with over 15,000 sold. Also with 6.5 million streams and 5.1 million in radio reach, it debuts at No. 27 on the Hot 100, more than a half-century after its 1974 release.

“9 to 5” (No. 16; 9.5 million streams, 7.2 million in airplay audience,15,000 sold), Parton’s Kenny Rogers duet “Islands in the Stream” (No. 26; 7.2 million streams, 4.2 million in audience,13,000 sold) and “Here You Come Again” (No. 44; 5 million streams, 2.9 million in audience, 10,000 sold) also reach the Hot 100.

An additional track, “Coat of Many Colors,” from 1971, appears on Hot Country Songs (No. 21; 4.5 million streams, 2.2 million in audience, 7,000 sold).

Along with Ultimate Dolly Parton on the Billboard 200, Parton appears with The Essential Dolly Parton (No. 85, 14,000 units). Diamonds & Rhinestones: The Greatest Hits Collection joins both sets on Top Country Albums (No. 41, 9,000 units).

More activity for Parton’s catalog will be reflected on the Sept. 12-dated Billboard charts covering the Aug. 28-Sept. 3 tracking week, the first full seven-day period after Parton’s death.
